name: Matthew Guo
headline: Hardware and systems engineer. Mountain View, CA.
summary: Hardware and systems engineer who owns multi-board compute and sensing platforms end to end: architecture and interface definition, schematic and layout, bring-up, cross-domain EE/firmware/mechanical debug on deployed fleets, EMI/SI root cause, and vendor-managed production. Founder of YAEDO Design House (boardmiko.com), a 5 to 10 engineer PCB design firm with its own EDA toolchain. Also builds and runs production trading systems and the risk and research infrastructure around them as Chief Investment Officer of Vosburg Capital.

experience.title: Hardware Engineer
highlights: Sole hardware engineer across multiple platforms; owns a distributed, high-bandwidth multi-board architecture (Intel Core Ultra compute, PCIe/Thunderbolt fabric) for a space-constrained L4 autonomous drone.

Architects and integrates the perception stack: multi-camera, lidar, optical-flow and inertial sensors, with interface, power and bandwidth budgets across compute, sensor and actuator subsystems including CAN.
Leads bring-up and cross-domain debug of new platform builds; chases integration faults to root cause and feeds fixes back into requirements and interface specs.
Designs versioned, fleet-manageable hardware: IQC, provisioning and flashing, revision traceability, field serviceability.

Root-causes and fixes EMI/SI failures on deployed PCIe and Thunderbolt hardware, often same day; introduced risk-management gates. Manages simulation and validation contractors and domestic and APAC design and EMS partners.

experience.title: Founder and Lead Engineer
highlights: Founded and leads a 5 to 10 engineer PCB design and hardware services firm; owns client scoping, requirements, schedule and delivery across client engineering, non-technical stakeholders and fab and assembly partners.
Built an automated quoting system that issues a binding, countersigned quote from submitted specs and files, backed by cost and effort models accurate enough to honor without manual review.

Built the firm's EDA toolchain: a patched KiCad fork with a guarded collaboration API, routers and escape generators, SI/PI review, a benchmarked decoupling placer, and client deliverable sites with fab packs.

experience.title: Electrical Engineer
highlights: Led all in-house PCB projects (10+ assemblies including IPC Class 3) and a custom NVIDIA Orin carrier that resolved sensor-bandwidth bottlenecks for on-robot AI processing.

Integrated and debugged controls, power, CAN, wiring and industrial sensing (encoders, laser and optical, safety and specialty sensors) on FANUC and ABB truss-assembly lines; fault-tolerant control architecture and device-scale UPS modules cut controls-related downtime 10x.
Deployed and managed a fleet of Yocto-based embedded Linux controllers with versioned provisioning, flashing and update workflows.
Cut subsystem BOM cost 20 percent and assembly time in half via custom modules and contract harness manufacturers; introduced phase-gating, DFM review and HALT/HASS validation.

Portfolio of disclosed Botbuilt boards (eleven, 2023 to 2025) is in the projects list: CM4 PCIe-to-USB3 breakout, 24 V output board, truss-arm controller and TMC262 driver modules, quadrature bridge, IoT storage controller, CM4 interposer with supercap hold-up, LED light ring, connection board, Input Table IO, Orin carrier.

experience.title: Mechatronics and Software Intern
highlights: Modeled and solved EMI and power-distribution issues on the truss line; introduced CI for embedded firmware with hardware-in-the-loop deployment.

experience.title: Chief Investment Officer
highlights: Long/short equity in hard technology. Built the firm's research, execution and risk infrastructure from scratch: two broker engines, a pre-registered research program and a parquet data lake.

education.status: Enrollment deferred to pursue full-time hardware engineering roles.

projects.name: Intel Panther Lake system-on-module
projects.what: Solo-architected next-generation autonomous drone motherboard around the Intel Core Ultra 9 (Panther Lake) SoC; about 90 percent of the schematic captured by hand: Thunderbolt 4 / PCIe 5 topology, LPDDR5X, iMVP9.3 PMIC, multi-level NVDC power delivery.

projects.name: Firefly automation controller
projects.what: Industrial controller around a Raspberry Pi Compute Module 5 with an STM32H743 co-processor: dual GbE (KSZ9893 switch, LAN7800), 2x USB 3.0 via a CYUSB3304 hub, M.2 B-key and M-key PCIe Gen3 with a PCIe mux and clock buffer, 2x HDMI 2.0, 22-pin MIPI CSI/DSI, isolated dual-channel IO-Link master (MAX14819 with MAX14931/14930 isolators) on M12-5P, USB-C sink and USB-C programming, FTDI UART, ideal-diode PPS front end taking 8 to 60 V to 5 V/5 A and 3.3 V/3 A rails. SI-aware PCIe/GbE/USB3 layout on 4 layers. Owned definition, bring-up, manufacture and go-to-market.
projects.status: Shipped; self-funded 0.5 to 1k-unit batches (Paisley Microsystems). Firefly-5 is the current generation; Firefly-4 preceded it.

projects.name: RK3588S compact board
projects.what: Chip-down RK3588S with onboard DDR5 on the smallest RK3588 footprint in the industry; full schematic, layout and bring-up.

projects.name: PCIe to USB 3.0 breakout for Raspberry Pi CM4
projects.what: Renesas uPD720201 PCIe-to-USB3 bridge with custom EEPROM config for CM4 kernels; four USB 3.0 ports sharing a 5 Gbps PCIe link, gigabit Ethernet, 20-pin JST I/O, 24 V input, 72 mm DIN-rail profile. 4-layer 1/0.5 oz FR-4, impedance controlled on 2116x3 resin cores. Used for Intel RealSense data collection on robot elbows and end effectors.

projects.name: 24 V digital output board
projects.what: 16 open-collector 24 V-tolerant outputs at 2 A continuous sink for solenoids, linear motors and contactors from 3.3 V logic. Single-sided 2-layer assembly. 35 units across 5 production lines with one hardware fault in a year: 72.8k hour demonstrated MTBF.

projects.name: Truss-building arm controller, rev 1 and rev 2
projects.what: Four-axis (X, Y, theta, clamp) stepper controller around an STM32F; 1/256 microstepping at over 250 W per channel, electromagnets and break-beam sensors in a hostile-EMI cell. 42 to 60 V hot-swap input, mezzanine motor-driver modules. Rev 2 puts the Raspberry Pi CM4 on board with CM4-IO-standard I/O, Ethernet and USB. 4-layer; rev 2 impedance controlled. 45 USD per unit at 20.

projects.name: Stepper driver mezzanine (TMC262)
projects.what: Single bipolar-stepper module, 44 to 60 V, 250 W sustained (2.8 A RMS per coil) with active cooling; rev 2 shrank the module and moved the motor connector on board. 4-layer 2/1 oz. 9.50 USD per unit at 30.

projects.name: Quadrature-to-digital protocol bridge
projects.what: Dedicated processor counts delta and direction of four quadrature encoders at once and exposes them over I2C and UART; RS-422 adapter for industrial encoders. 2-layer, low cost, small form factor.

projects.name: IoT workplace storage unit controller
projects.what: Wireless module, load-cell analog front end with a sub-0.75 mV ripple regulator at 1.3 MHz, four 12 V pass-through inputs for daisy-chaining, USB-C UART, peak-power scheme for a high-current solenoid. 4-layer. Under 16 USD assembled at 50 units.

projects.name: CM4 SBC interposer with power hold-up
projects.what: Sits between a CM4 and its carrier; supercapacitor bank gives time for a clean shutdown on power loss via a hardware flag, zero-dropout changeover between main and backup supplies. Quad-SPI SD and octal-SPI Samsung eMMC behind a repurposed Ethernet mux, USB-C flashing without a carrier. 6-layer 1/0.5/0.5 oz, impedance controlled, 0.4 mm-pitch BGA. 26.80 USD per unit at 50.

projects.name: High-power LED light ring for computer vision
projects.what: 4.5 W ring within USB 2.0 power budget, digitally controlled brightness and colour temperature. Rev 1: ATtiny1616 as I2C slave driving the LED driver; rev 2: STM32F4, TPS61181 boost driver, STUSB4500 USB-C PD sink, FT230X UART, potentiometer plus LMC555 manual mode, SWD programming. 2-layer, 88 parts, flush heatsink mounting. Deployed on every production line.

projects.name: Truss electronics connection board
projects.what: Ordered breakout for the Nucleo-based development truss platform, replacing hundreds of hand-spliced DuPont wires; 1206 parts for hand soldering, 24 hours from tape-out to fabricated boards.

projects.name: Input Table IO solution
projects.what: Two-part DIN-rail assembly (logic main board plus front-panel connector board over a right-angle DIN 41612) reading multiple motor encoders and driving a REAJET industrial printer with push-pull 24 V encoder signals; ADuM1201 isolation, TXS0108 level shifting, ULN2002 and L293 drivers, SMAJ26A transient protection, M8 and M12 field connectors, Nucleo-F410 processor. 4-layer, 90 parts. Replaced 3.5k USD of off-the-shelf industrial I/O per system with under 0.8k USD across 5 lines.

projects.name: NVIDIA Orin carrier
projects.what: Custom carrier resolving sensor-bandwidth bottlenecks for on-robot AI processing on FANUC/ABB truss-assembly lines.

projects.name: Kintex-7 capture board
projects.what: 8-layer, ~206x120 mm, XC7K325T FFG676, 72 LVCMOS25 lines at 50 MHz DDR over two Hirose FX10A-144, 2x SFP+ 10GBASE-R, USB 3.2 on GTX, DDR3, HDMI, FT4232H, USB-C PD. ~820 parts, 12.5k tracks, 3.2k vias, 0 DRC errors at last readiness check.

projects.name: Flex extension family
